class_id: a 200 response with zero rows read as "no data" rather than "broken call"
feature: scraper/src/scrapers/chittorgarh-scraper.ts (report-82 list endpoint) and any list-report fetch whose page size is a caller-supplied number
symptom: Chittorgarh report 82 accepts EXACTLY ONE page size. Measured read-only against the live endpoint 2026-09-11: perPage=10 returns HTTP 200 with all 231 rows (the report ignores the page size), while perPage=20/50/100/300 each return HTTP 200 with zero rows and error "Invalid API Call<year>-<perPage>-01". The failure carries a success status, so an empty list reads as "no IPOs today" instead of "this call is malformed". fetchChittorgarhAPI's default perPage was 100 - a call that returns nothing - and never fired only because its single caller passed 10 by hand; the code comment beside it stated "API accepts perPage: 10, 20, 30...", which is false and actively invites the change that breaks it.
first_seen: Sep 2026, found while wiring item 2 slice 7 (issue_type from report 82). Never fired in production: latent behind one hand-written argument.
fix_prs: #569 (page size named REPORT82_PAGE_SIZE with the measurement in its comment, made the default, misleading comment corrected)
detection_check: scraper/tests/unit/scrapers/chittorgarh-report82-page-size.test.ts - pins the constant to 10 and asserts it is none of the four values measured to return zero rows. Mutation-checked: restoring the old default of 100 turns both tests red. NOT a runtime check - a cycle that receives zero rows already raises via the existing `error` branch in scrapeChittorgarhIPOs, so the gap this closes is the source-level one, where the value looks like a harmless tuning knob.
